about.intro: I'm a creative technologist in Montreal. I make AI video for advertising, and I build the tools that keep it on brand.
bio: My work runs the whole way from concept to generated shots, image-to-video, client revisions and the finished spot. Alongside it I write custom ComfyUI nodes in Python that fix what makes AI footage unusable in a real job: characters that drift between shots, environments that change, logos that come out garbled.

I trained in VFX (FX TD diploma, Campus VFX, Montreal, 2023–2024), which is where the pipeline thinking comes from. Before that I spent seven years at Emirates as cabin crew, ending in Business Class: premium client service, and staying calm under pressure, every day. Most recently I worked in IT operations at oXya (2024–2026).
Since June 2025 I've been freelancing for production teams in Saudi Arabia, delivering AI imagery and video inside productions that also use CGI and VFX.

projects.title: Client work for Saudi production teams
projects.tagline: AI imagery and video inside real productions, alongside CGI and VFX.
projects.summary: Half the visuals of a ten-minute presentation film, historical scenes for a promotional film, destination views for a rail campaign, and shots an earlier VFX approach couldn't deliver.
projects.brief: Since June 2025 I've worked freelance with production teams in Saudi Arabia, delivering AI imagery and video inside productions that also use CGI and conventional VFX. Clients aren't named here, so each job is described by what it needed.
what_i_did: Produced about half the visuals of a ten-minute presentation film that mixes AI imagery, video generation, CGI and VFX.

Built historical environments and characters for a promotional film, revising frames from detailed cultural notes (architecture, wardrobe, crowd density, props) before converting the approved frames to video.
Made destination backgrounds for a rail campaign: replaced the window views in photographed train interiors and matched the lighting to the carriage and the passengers.
Rescued shots an earlier VFX approach couldn't deliver: a head-through-ceiling gag, a frozen performer with only his headscarf moving, and a camera move extended into a transition.

projects.title: NOVARA
projects.tagline: A spec ad for a fictional Milan espresso brand, made entirely in ComfyUI on a 10 GB GPU.
projects.summary: Spec ad for a fictional Milan espresso brand, made entirely in ComfyUI on a 10 GB GPU: brief to MP4 through my own planning, critique and repair nodes.
projects.brief: NOVARA is a spec ad for a fictional Milan espresso brand, made entirely in ComfyUI on a 10 GB GPU. The point is the pipeline: a brief goes in, and every stage that usually breaks AI advertising (the customer changing face between shots, the logo melting, a weak shot slipping through) has a node that catches it.
what_i_did: Designed the pipeline end to end, brief to finished MP4.
Keyframes: generated the first shot, then edited each later shot from the previous one with Qwen Image Edit and a next-scene LoRA, so the same customer appears in every shot.
Built the Shot Critic: Gemini reviews every shot three times and takes a majority vote, then routes it.
Used Detail Fixer to repair the logo only on flagged shots, with a keep-better gate.
Made image-to-video switchable per shot: local Wan, local MiniMax H3, or API models such as Kling.

projects.title: ComfyUI-DetailFixer
projects.tagline: Fixes garbled logos, faces or any area you name in a generated image. Everything else stays untouched.
projects.summary: Open-source ComfyUI node: name an area, and it fixes only that area (a garbled logo, a face) while everything else stays untouched.
projects.brief: Generated images often get almost everything right and one thing wrong: the logo is garbled, a face is off. Regenerating the whole frame loses what was good. ComfyUI-DetailFixer fixes only the area you name. SAM 3 finds each area, an edit model regenerates just that area from a reference, and the result is blended back so the rest of the image is untouched.
what_i_did: Wrote the node in Python and published it as open source.
Used SAM 3 to find each named area: a logo, a face, anything you can describe.
Made the edit model switchable: local Qwen on a 10 GB GPU, or Nano Banana 2 / GPT Image 2 via API.
Blended each fix back so everything outside the area stays exactly as it was.

projects.title: ComfyUI-ShotPlanner
projects.tagline: Turns a brief or a script into a shot list with image and video prompts for every shot.
projects.summary: Open-source ComfyUI nodes: brief or script to shot list with image and video prompts per shot, then Shot Critic and Ad Assembler.
projects.brief: ComfyUI-ShotPlanner turns a brief or a script into a shot list, with an image prompt and a video prompt for every shot. It runs on Gemini, Claude or GPT, or offline. The same pack includes the Shot Critic, which reviews each generated shot and routes it, and the Ad Assembler, which cuts the shots into a finished ad. Together they are the planning and finishing ends of the NOVARA pipeline.
what_i_did: Wrote the nodes in Python and published them as open source.
Shot Planner: a brief or script in, a shot list out, with image and video prompts per shot.
Shot Critic: Gemini reviews every shot three times and takes a majority vote, routing each to pass, detail fix, consistency fix or re-render.
Ad Assembler: timeline, transitions, supers, end card and audio mix, out to MP4.
